title: Masked fat loss likely
summary: Fat loss may be occurring, but scale weight is likely being masked by water retention or short-term weight noise.
evidence: Calorie data suggests a deficit is present.
Observed weight loss is lower than expected.
recommendation: Hold calories steady for 7 more days before cutting further. Monitor the 7-day average rather than single weigh-ins.

title: Recovery masking likely
summary: Poor sleep or higher training load may be increasing short-term water retention and hiding fat loss on the scale.
evidence: Sleep quality or duration is below the target range.
recommendation: Keep the calorie target stable, reduce unnecessary training fatigue, and improve sleep consistency for the next week.

title: Adherence drift likely
summary: The apparent deficit may be weakened by inconsistent intake, weekend drift or incomplete logging.
evidence: Calories vary significantly across the week.
Weekend calorie intake is higher than weekday intake.
recommendation: Audit weekend intake, liquid calories, snacks, cooking oils and untracked extras before reducing calories further.

title: Reduced expenditure likely
summary: A drop in steps or activity may have reduced the real calorie deficit.
evidence: Average steps have dropped compared with the previous period.
Lower daily movement can reduce total expenditure.
recommendation: Restore step count before lowering calories. Aim for a consistent daily step floor.

title: Protein consistency risk
summary: Low or inconsistent protein intake may make the deficit harder to maintain and reduce diet quality.
evidence: Protein intake is below the target threshold.
Low protein can make hunger and adherence harder during a deficit.
recommendation: Increase protein consistency before making the deficit more aggressive.

title: True plateau possible
summary: A real plateau may be developing if the mismatch persists without strong masking signals.
evidence: There are fewer signs of short-term masking or calorie inconsistency.
recommendation: If this persists for another 7–14 days, consider a small calorie reduction or activity increase.
